name: Aminata Diallo
headline: 19-year-old apprentice bricklayer and part-time student, Bamako, Mali
title: A Walk to See School Bags
situation: On a Sunday afternoon, Aminata sits on her mat reviewing accounting notes. Her younger sister, Fatoumata, appears at the door and asks if Aminata will walk with her to the market to look at school bags. Fatoumata is not buying one, just wanting Aminata's opinion on which bag looks sturdy enough to last the year. The market is a forty-minute walk each way, and Aminata still has several pages of practice problems she wanted to finish before the lamp oil runs out. She could put down her notebook and go with her sister, or ask Fatoumata to go alone and come back later.

context.relationship_profiles: Aminata is Fatoumata's guardian and sole family, having raised her since their mother's death. Fatoumata depends on Aminata for guidance and rarely makes decisions without her approval.
context.tendencies: When study time conflicts with Fatoumata's requests, Aminata has sometimes finished a set number of problems before leaving, but other times she has set her notebook aside to avoid disappointing her sister.
context.current_state: She is two hours into reviewing and has six practice problems left; the lamp oil will last another ninety minutes. Her shoulders ache from the week's labor, and she is focused but not urgent.
context.immediate_memories: Hearing 'school bags' reminds her of the cheap canvas bag she carried as a child that tore after two months, forcing her to carry books in her arms.
context.reflective_memories: She recalls walking her mother to the market stall every Saturday before the loan default, when her mother would say that showing up is half the work.
